builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
summary: The technique replaces standard KGQA fine-tuning that only checks final answer strings, substituting a training pipeline where questions are synthesized with verifiable supporting triples and agents receive process rewards for retrieving them. It requires building an evidence-grounded data synthesis pipeline and an interaction agent that logs retrieved triples per turn, adding engineering complexity to the training loop. If the synthesized sub-questions fail to align with the target KG schema or the reward is misattributed to intermediate turns, the agent may learn to game the coverage metric without improving factual accuracy.
rationale: The method targets a specific production need—auditable evidence retrieval with small open models—but requires validation on your specific KG schema and workload before replacing established RAG or fine-tuning pipelines.
technique: Evidence-grounded KG agent training with coverage rewards

claims.statement: The technique replaces standard KGQA fine-tuning that only checks final answer strings, substituting a training pipeline where questions are synthesized with verifiable supporting triples and agents receive process rewards for retrieving them. It requires building an evidence-grounded data synthesis pipeline and an interaction agent that logs retrieved triples per turn, adding engineering complexity to the training loop. If the synthesized sub-questions fail to align with the target KG schema or the reward is misattributed to intermediate turns, the agent may learn to game the coverage metric without improving factual accuracy.
FoG enables 3B--4B open-source agents to outperform substantially larger baselines in answer accuracy and evidence coverage, with zero-shot cross-KG transfer.
